name: Mt. Davidson
notes: In Mt. Davidson Park. Mount Davidson Cross is at the top. 270 degree views close by at Mount Davidson Vista Point.

name: Noe Peak
notes: South Twin Peak. 360 degree views.

name: Signal Point
notes: In Signal Point Park. 360 degree views by walking around the park.

name: Bayview Hill (Candlestick Hill)
notes: In Bayview Park. Views at the summit are obstructed by trees but the loop trail near the top offers good views in all directions.

name: Forest Hill
notes: Residential. Off-limits water tank at the top.

name: Visitacion Knob (McLaren Ridge)
notes: In John McLaren Park. Views mostly obscured by trees.

name: Potrero Hill
notes: Residential.

name: Bernal Hill
notes: In Bernal Heights Park. Telecommunications tower equipment on top but can get 360 degree views by walking around it.

name: Merced Heights
notes: In Lakeview and Ashton Mini Park. 360 degree views.

name: Mount Sutro
notes: In the Mount Sutro Open Space Reserve. Forested.

name: Lincoln Heights
notes: In front of the Legion of Honor. Views obstructed by trees.

name: Stony Hill (Hunters Point Ridge)
notes: Next to a preschool. Residential. Better views at Hilltop Park close by (which also has a large sundial).

name: Telegraph Hill
notes: In Pioneer Park. Views partially obstructed by trees on all sides. For good views ascend Coit Tower for a fee.

name: Strawberry Hill
notes: An island inside Blue Heron Lake in Golden Gate Park. Mostly unobstructed views to the north and south.

name: Nob Hill
notes: Hilltop is on the pedestrian-only Priest Street. No view as it is obstructed by buildings.

name: Edgehill Heights
notes: Residential.

name: Mount St. Joseph
notes: Residential. Small public area nearby between 290 and 300 Bayview Circle with 90 degree views.

name: Lone Mountain
notes: On the University of San Francisco campus. 180 degree views to the south.

name: Lafayette Heights
notes: In Lafayette Park. Mostly unobstructed views if you walk past the trees on the top.

name: Gold Mine Hill
notes: Residential. Some partially obstructed views.

name: Presidio Hill
notes: Inside the Presidio of San Francisco. Inaccessible due to a municipal water storage basin and WVY transmitter station on the summit. Nearest public access is from the Presidio Golf Course with decent southward views; nearest free access is along the Bay Area Ridge Trail.

name: Buena Vista Heights
notes: In Buena Vista Park. View almost completely obstructed by trees.

name: Corona Heights
notes: In Corona Heights Park. 360 degree views.

name: Castro Hill
notes: Residential.

name: Cannon Hill
notes: Residential. Just outside the Presidio of San Francisco.

name: Rob Hill
notes: Just outside Rob Hill Campground in the Presidio of San Francisco. Obstructed views. Summit under construction as of April 2026.

name: Russian Hill
notes: Right above Ina Coolbrith Park. 180 degree views.

name: Rincon Hill
notes: Urban. Located at the entrance of the One Rincon Hill condominium complex. Next to Interstate 80.

name: Mount Olympus
notes: In the very small Mount Olympus Park. Pedestal of the former Triumph of Light statue on top. Some views but mostly surrounded by houses.

name: Eureka Peak
notes: North Twin Peak. 360 degree views.

name: Clarendon Heights
notes: Sutro Tower at the top is off-limits. Closest access is from the Sutro Tower Trail.

name: Dolores Heights
notes: Residential.

name: Grand View Hill
notes: In Grandview Park. 360 degree views with few trees.

name: Red Rock Hill
notes: Inside the Diamond Heights Village Association. No view.

name: Fairmount Heights
notes: Residential. 180 degree views.

name: Anza Hill
notes: Residential.

name: Laurel Hill
notes: Residential.

name: Prayerbrook Cross Hill
notes: In Golden Gate Park. Prayerbrook Cross is at the top, and Rainbow Falls descends down its southern slope. Partially obstructed views to the south.

name: Holly Hill
notes: Flat top but can get views from all directions by walking around it.

name: La Portezuela
notes: Residential. Views to the northeast from the end of the road. The summit is only a few meters from the city boundary so whether it lies in San Francisco or Daly City is debatable.

name: Madrid Hill
notes: Residential.

name: Alamo Heights (Hayes Hill)
notes: Near Alamo Square and the Painted Ladies.

name: Macaroon Hill
notes: Residential.

name: Blue Tower Hill
notes: In John McLaren Park. 180 degree views to the northwest.

name: Martha Hill
notes: In Dorothy W. Erskine Park. 180 degree views.

name: Crocker Amazon Hill
notes: In John McLaren Park. 360 degree views.

name: Horner's Hill
notes: Residential.

name: Pasadena Hill
notes: Inaccessible due to private property. Closest access is on Pasadena St.

name: Hunter's Point Shipyard Hill
notes: Residential. Southwestward views from nearby Hillpoint Park.

name: Little Bayview Hill (Tubsinte Hill)
notes: Residential. Next to Little Hollywood Park.

name: Monterey Heights
notes: Residential.

name: City College Hill
notes: On the City College of San Francisco campus. Science Hall occupies the summit. Walking around the building provides views to the west, north, and east.

name: Amuctac Hill
notes: In John McLaren Park. 180 degree views to the south.

name: George Sterling Park
notes: By Lombard Street. Residential.

name: Battery Davis
notes: In Fort Funston. The summit is on top of a historic concrete gun emplacement. Views are partially obstructed by trees.

name: Torpedo Point
notes: Below Interstate 80. Top is inaccessible due to military use. Closest public access is along the pedestrian pathway on the southeast side of the hill.

name: Seal Rocks
notes: An island. Inaccessible but can be viewed from the shore.

name: Larsen Peak (Sunset Heights)
notes: In Golden Gate Heights Park. Views partially obstructed by trees on all sides.

name: Irish Hill
notes: Inaccessible due to private property. The closest public access is on Michigan St.

name: Pacheco Peak
notes: Residential.

name: Mount Lick
notes: In Golden Gate Park. Views obstructed by trees.

name: Battery Dynamite
notes: In the Presidio of San Francisco. Restricted access. Closest access is from Ralston Avenue.

name: Chicken Point
notes: In Golden Gate Park. Views obstructed by trees.

name: Casino Hill
notes: In Golden Gate Park. Views obstructed by trees.

name: Fort Mason Hill
notes: In Fort Mason Park. Views in all directions are available by walking around the park.

name: Cathedral Hill
notes: At the Cathedral of Saint Mary of the Assumption. The cathedral's decks offer views to the south that are partially obstructed by buildings.

name: Kite Hill
notes: In Kite Hill. 180 degree views.

name: Billy Goat Hill
notes: In Billy Goat Hill. 180 degree views.

name: Alcatraz Island
notes: Access requires a paid ferry ticket. The summit is near the lighthouse. Good views in all directions are available by walking around the island.

name: Sutro Heights
notes: In Sutro Heights Park. 180 degree views to the south.

name: Tank Hill
notes: In Tank Hill Park. 270 degree views.

name: Hawk Hill
notes: Inaccessible as of May 2026.

name: Heidelberg Hill
notes: Inside the San Francisco Botanical Garden in Golden Gate Park. Requires paying the garden entrance fee (free for San Francisco residents). Partially obstructed views to the south.

name: Hermit Rock
notes: An island. Inaccessible but can be viewed from the shore.

name: Alta Plaza Park
notes: In Alta Plaza Park. Southward views; northward views obstructed by buildings.

name: Duncan Hill
notes: In Duncan & Castro Open Space. 180 degree views.

name: Ignatius Heights
notes: On the University of San Francisco campus. No views.
